clue.text: Cracking up 30 across

indicators.note: up can mean in disorder or astir, so the letters of the other answer are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the clue points to the answer at 30 across, whose letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone is breaking down under the strain of putting things right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' shuffles STRAIGHTEN, the answer to 30 across; the two answers are anagrams of each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shattering is splitting into fragments, just as a cracking pane breaks apart.

clue.text: Lay off the drink!

explanation.surface: An order to stop boozing.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay off workers is to dismiss them, and sack was an old dry white wine like sherry.

clue.text: Find a welcome carrying people's correspondence

indicators.note: one word holds another inside it, as a bearer carries a load

parts.note: to welcome someone is to greet them
men is a common word for people in crosswords

explanation.surface: Looking for a friendly reception for someone's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence in the sense of matching or concord is accord between things.

clue.text: A topic to get the meeting started

indicators.note: only the start of the words is taken, the opening five letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: Suggesting a subject to open a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'started' takes the opening letters of 'the meeting', which spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or main idea under discussion.

clue.text: Free about fifty with a certain nonchalance

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for concerning or about
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
ease of manner is a relaxed nonchalance

explanation.surface: Liberating fifty people with an air of casual indifference.
explanation.definitionFit: To free a prisoner is to let them go, to set them loose.

clue.text: Most stingy and earnest characters in need of a break

indicators.note: the letters want breaking up and putting back together in another order

explanation.surface: A miser who works earnestly and badly needs a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters in need of a break' says the letters of EARNEST are broken and reset.
explanation.definitionFit: Near can mean mean with money, so the most near is the tightest-fisted.

clue.text: State service

explanation.surface: A two-word note about public service.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass is short for Massachusetts, a US state, and the Mass is a Catholic church service.

clue.text: Sound forecaster doing a boring job

indicators.note: the clue's opening word tells us to go by how a word is said, not spelt

parts.note: an augur was a Roman priest who foretold events

explanation.surface: A reliable weather prophet stuck in dull work.
explanation.definitionFit: An auger is a tool for drilling holes, so it literally bores.

clue.text: Viewers should hold on to catch "The Poets"

indicators.note: the first word must hold the others inside it, like a container

parts.note: seers are those who see, viewers
taken as written
to net a fish is to catch it

explanation.surface: Television audiences should stay tuned for a programme called The Poets.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonneteers are writers of fourteen-line sonnets, a kind of poet.

clue.text: Stony feline look

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun naming a stone

parts.note: a tiger is a big feline
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A big cat's hard, cold stare.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger-eye is a golden-brown quartz gemstone, so it belongs among stones.

clue.text: A number in trouble? That could be grave

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: care means worry or trouble
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A count of people in difficulty might mean a serious situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' is an old verb meaning to engrave or cut, not the adjective it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To grave is the archaic form of engrave, to cut into stone or wood.

clue.text: Enticing a dog in to rest

indicators.note: the dog goes inside the word for rest

parts.note: to lean is to rest against something
a dingo is a wild Australian dog

explanation.surface: Coaxing a dog indoors so it will settle down.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading someone on is luring or tempting them, often deceptively.

clue.text: Prizing for example a merry party on retirement

indicators.note: retiring is drawing back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: a revel is a lively celebration

explanation.surface: A jolly party thrown for someone leaving work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prizing' means forcing open (prising), not valuing; 'on retirement' turns EGAREVEL round.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage is the use of a lever to force something open or move it.

clue.text: The retreat of a real high-flier

definitions.text: The retreat of a real high-flier

parts.words: The retreat of a real high-flier
parts.note: a high-flier is usually a successful person, but here a literal one: a bird of prey and its lofty home

explanation.surface: A successful executive's private hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's nest built high on a crag is its refuge.

clue.text: To effect some improvement in appearance is encouraging

parts.note: a coming is an arrival or appearance
to mend is to repair or improve

explanation.surface: Smartening up one's looks is a good sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Commending someone is praising them, which heartens and spurs them on.

clue.text: Took in more than necessary because of a note

parts.note: over in the sense of on account of, as in a row over money
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone absorbed too much information because of one written message.
explanation.definitionFit: To overeat is to consume more food than one needs.

clue.text: Neat code worked out by 24 across

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cipher cracked by a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short story, and 24 across in its narrative sense means a telling of events.

clue.text: A machine-operator entering parliament read letters aloud

indicators.note: the answer goes into the run of words and sits within them

explanation.surface: An MP reading out correspondence in the House.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in 'parliamenT READ LEtters'; 'aloud' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot pedal that drives a machine such as a sewing machine or lathe.

clue.text: Untrustworthy but attractive girl with love-nest

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
love is zero in tennis, written as O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shady character with a beauty in a cosy hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishonest person cannot be relied on to tell the truth.

clue.text: Doesn't convey a clear message say in writing

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A note that fails to get its meaning across.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who mutters speaks indistinctly, so the words are hard to catch.

clue.text: A crawler among the stars

parts.note: a crawler sounds like a toady among celebrities, but it is a creeping creature that is also a constellation

explanation.surface: A sycophant in the company of celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake creeps along the ground, and Serpens, a constellation, is named for one.

clue.text: The unctuous guy rages wildly with little hesitation

indicators.note: wildly says the letters run riot into another order

parts.note: er is a brief pause in speech

explanation.surface: An oily man losing his temper, then faltering a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A greaser is an oily flatterer, or in slang a smooth, slick sort of man.

clue.text: Festive meal for a Greek maid

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion
tea is an afternoon or evening meal

explanation.surface: A celebratory spread laid on for a young woman from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Galatea is the statue brought to life in Greek myth, and a sea nymph of legend.

clue.text: Important though not top pressman

parts.note: the editor, ED, is the chief of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A significant figure, yet not the leading journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A noted person is well known and of some standing.

clue.text: Gradually reduce the light

explanation.surface: Advice to turn down the lamp slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: To taper is to narrow by degrees, and a taper is a thin candle giving light.

clue.text: Member of the family presenting-an account

explanation.surface: A relative giving a report.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is a kinsman, and also a narration or telling of events.

clue.text: Disturbed night? Object!

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed into another order

explanation.surface: Someone woken in the dark crying out in protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb of protest but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is any physical item or article.

clue.text: A fellow given a little latitude and rightly so

indicators.note: the fellow is given only a little of the next words, a short run of letters from inside them

explanation.surface: A colleague allowed some leeway, deservedly.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in 'latituDE ANd rightly so', near the start of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean is a senior fellow of a college with charge of discipline.

clue.text: Converts apt in time to get restless

indicators.note: the letters are converted into another order

explanation.surface: Religious converts grow fidgety waiting for the right moment.
explanation.definitionFit: An impatient person is fidgety and eager, unwilling to wait.

clue.text: A woman showing displeasure about a couple of points

parts.note: ire is anger or displeasure
N and E are two compass points

explanation.surface: A lady cross about two details.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a female first name.

clue.text: Talk without the right-it's habit

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: gab is chatter or talk

explanation.surface: Chatting improperly is a bad habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a monk's or nun's robe, a kind of clothing.

clue.text: Sort out 1 across

indicators.note: out can mean in disarray, so the fodder's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the clue points to the answer at 1 across, whose letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: An instruction to fix a crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles SHATTERING, the answer to 1 across.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort things is to put them in order, to tidy them up.
